description: 2 tactical challenges for Black against the Slav Gambit. Hold with 4...b5! or develop with 4...Nf6!.

drills.briefExplanation: 3...dxc4 4.e4 b5! 5.a4 b4 — take, hold, and push past the undermining.
drills.description: Black to play. White plays into the Slav — take on c4 and hold with 4...b5!.
drills.explanation: The greedy defense: after 3.Nc3 dxc4, Black holds the pawn with 4...b5!. White's 4.e4 is met with a solid queenside wall — the c4 pawn is defended, the b5 pawn controls a4, and Black is a clean pawn up. Holding gambit pawns takes nerve; the b5 push provides it.
drills.name: Holding the Pawn

drills.briefExplanation: 4...Nf6! 5.e5 Nd5 6.Nxd5 cxd5 — develop with tempo, blockade, and trade.
drills.description: Black to play. White struck with 4.e4 — develop with tempo via 4...Nf6!.
drills.explanation: The active defense: 4...Nf6! develops while attacking e4. After 5.e5 Nd5 Black's knight lands on its dream outpost — blockading the e-pawn, eyeing c3 and f4, impossible to chase. White's 'gambit' center is frozen, Black is a pawn up, and the knight on d5 is worth the price of admission.
drills.name: The Nd5 Blockade

name: Slav Gambit — Black Tactics
